completed_proof_deductions: On a smooth factorial complex threefold with primitive nonzero LND, polynomial two-dimensional kernel and faithfully flat quotient, the induced derivation is nonzero on every whole scheme-theoretic quotient fiber. At a closed fiber it is already nonzero on the local scheme of each component's generic point. It may vanish on the reduction.

The local proof uses a transverse Artinian complete intersection, the characteristic-zero Jacobian socle theorem and regularity of the multiplier between the local Jacobian field and primitive D. No rational component field or global volume is assumed.

Combining this nonvanishing theorem with the exact pass53 inclusion D(F5) in mF4 proves R[F5] proper in the actual algebra in the reduced zero-first-jet sector. Every generating set there requires intrinsic degree at least six, and (a,b) is not regular on the full K5 algebra.

The actual slices form an affine coset H_*+A_R in L[j]. Existence of a projected F5 list is equivalent to that coset meeting degree at most two and equivalent to a projected F4 list. This does not characterize every possible low-degree generating set.

Actual replica automorphisms exp(r^N E), with explicit polynomial inverses, give unbounded arbitrary supplied-slice degrees in every actual instance, but preserve the selection coset. They do not refute an existential low-degree choice.
The cofactor original-flow bound and constant-iterate shortcut were deduplicated against earlier results. They do not supply a minimum intrinsic generating-degree upper bound.
